newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends slightly up after dull trading.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends slightly up after dull trading.

text.p: The won closed slightly higher against the dollar on Tuesday after dull trading, affected by intervention from the central Bank of Korea, dealers said.
Dealers said the central bank sold dollars to slow the local currency's drop. But the central bank has never confirmed that it intervenes in the interbank market.
"The dollar showed little movement in the afternoon as most banks covered their short dollar positions after the central bank's dollar selling," said one dealer.
The won ended at 844.70 after opening the day at 844.90.
The market will be closed for trading on Christmas Day.
Dealers have said the central bank wanted to keep the dollar's ceiling capped at below 845 won level for the rest of this year.
But the continued export slump has put the local currency under downward pressure, they said.
"With the current market situation, I doubt the 845 won ceiling will be kept by the year-end," said another dealer.
Dealers forecast the won's base mid-rate was expected to be set at 844.70 for Thursday, compared with Tuesday's 844.30.
